newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Up to 40 said killed in Cambodia after overthrow.
newsitem.headline: Up to 40 said killed in Cambodia after overthrow.

text.p: As many as 40 Cambodians may have been killed for political reasons in the wake of this month's overthrow of First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh, a diplomatic source said on Wednesday.

The source, who declined to be identified, said there was evidence some victims had been tortured, including four bodyguards of Ranariddh's top military commander, General Nhiek Bun Chhay, who were found with their eyes gouged out.
"It doesn't seem to be good," the source said of the human rights situation since Second Prime Minister Hun Sen's coup against his co-premier and coalition partner Ranariddh.
"There seem to have been 40 deaths that one could say with relative safety were politically motivated," the source said.

While attacks on officials from Ranariddh's FUNCINPEC party appeared to be going on across the country, the figure of 40 deaths had been compiled mostly from incidents in the Phnom Penh area although it was not clear if the killings were part of a planned purge, he said.
"It's very unclear if this is a centrally orchestrated, carefully planned purge or more dispersed -- a general uncoordinated attack on FUNCINPEC officials," he said.
"But even if it is the latter, it could be stopped," he said.
King Norodom Sihanouk on Tuesday accused Hun Sen's police and troops of torturing and killing political opponents and urged an end to the bloodshed.

"I am profoundly distressed at the reports that the military and members of the national police have cruelly tortured and killed without mercy their enemies after having arrested or captured them," Sihanouk said in a letter sent from Beijing to acting head of state Chea Sim in Phnom Penh.

Government officials have confirmed the death of two senior FUNCINPEC officials, one of them Ho Sok, a secretary of state at the Interior Ministry who was arrested by Hun Sen's troops and subsequently shot dead by "angry armed men".
The other, Chao Sambath, a FUNCINPEC intelligence officer, was killed during fighting in the capital on July 5-6, Hun Sen said this week.

Both men were on a list of four people who Hun Sen blamed for the fighting and said had to be hunted down and arrested. The other two, Nhiek Bun Chhay and Ranariddh's top security adviser, Serey Kosal, have not been reported captured.
International human rights groups said they had grave fears for the safety of hundreds of royalist soldiers and supporters captured during the fighting.
Military officials denied they were being mistreated and said they were undergoing "re-education".
Sihanouk, who reigns but does not rule in Cambodia, reminded the government in his letter to Chea Sim that the law and the constitution absolutely forbid torture and murder.
